sections.heading: Native or Cross-Platform: Which Is Right for You?
paragraphs: One of the first decisions in any app project is whether to build two native apps or one cross-platform app. There is no universally right answer, and we will explain the trade-offs for your specific product rather than push one option.

Native development (Kotlin for Android, Swift for iOS) gives the best performance and the deepest access to device features. It is usually the right choice for apps that rely heavily on the camera, sensors, Bluetooth, complex animations or offline processing, and for products where a polished platform-specific experience is part of the value.

Cross-platform development (Flutter or React Native) shares most of the code between Android and iOS. For the majority of business apps, such as booking, ordering, loyalty, content, field-service and marketplace apps, it delivers a high-quality experience at a lower cost, with one team maintaining one codebase. It also makes it easier to keep both versions in step when you add features.
During discovery we look at your features, budget, timeline and long-term plans, and recommend the approach that gives you the best product for the money.

sections.heading: What Affects the Cost of an App
paragraphs: We do not publish a single price for app development, because two apps with similar names can differ several times over in effort. The main factors are:
list: The number of screens and features in the first version
Native Android and iOS apps or one cross-platform app
Whether you need a custom backend, an admin panel or integration with existing systems
Payments, maps, chat, video, offline use or other complex features
The level of custom design and animation
Ongoing maintenance and support after launch
after: The most cost-effective route is usually a focused first version that solves the core problem well, launched quickly and improved based on real feedback. We will help you decide what belongs in that first release and what can wait. After the discovery call you receive a written estimate, so there are no surprises later.

items.q: How long does it take to build a mobile app?
items.a: A focused first version usually takes a few months from discovery to launch. Simple apps can be faster, and apps with complex backends, integrations or many user roles take longer. You get a timeline with the written scope.

items.q: Should I build for Android or iOS first?
items.a: In India, Android has a much larger share of users, so many businesses start there or build both at once with a cross-platform framework. If your target audience is mainly iPhone users, or you serve markets like Australia, iOS may matter more. We look at your audience before recommending.

items.q: Do I own the source code?
items.a: Yes. On final payment the source code, designs and all project assets belong to you, and the apps are published under your own developer accounts.

items.q: Can you build an app for my existing website or Shopify store?
items.a: Yes. We can connect the app to your existing website, WordPress site or Shopify store so products, customers and orders stay in sync.

items.q: Will you help with publishing on Google Play and the App Store?
items.a: Yes. We prepare the listings, screenshots and privacy details, submit the app and handle any feedback from the store review teams.

items.q: Do you provide support after launch?
items.a: Yes. We offer monthly maintenance plans that cover bug fixes, OS compatibility updates, monitoring, security patches and small improvements, with larger features quoted separately.

items.q: Can you take over an app built by another developer?
items.a: Usually, yes. We start with a code review to assess quality and risks, then recommend whether to continue with the existing code, refactor parts of it or rebuild.
